method: ENTIRELY from AMH's General principles: anti-infectives page, read under subscription and PARAPHRASED: no passage reproduced, no source_text stored, so NOTHING here is machine re-checkable. This is a PRINCIPLES page: it names no organism-drug pairing and sets no specific regimen, and this guideline does not invent either. ⚠️ AMH's own Drug choice for selected infections page and its nine organism-susceptibility tables were NOT retrieved, and Therapeutic Guidelines -- the Australian source that would answer 'which drug for which bug' -- is licensed and not held in this compendium. What this guideline carries is the stewardship framework: when not to prescribe, how long, and which drugs to leave alone.

claims.claim: Indications listed in AMH's anti-infective monographs ARE NOT COMPREHENSIVE and are OFTEN MUCH MORE LIMITED THAN THE MARKETED INDICATIONS; they are based on clinical practice and evidence for appropriate use and MAY INCLUDE NON-MARKETED USES
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'General principles: anti-infectives' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/anti-infectives/general-principles-anti-infectives, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: USE ANTI-INFECTIVES ONLY WHERE THERE IS CLEAR EVIDENCE OR STRONG SUSPICION OF AN INFECTION THAT WILL NOT RESOLVE UNAIDED: many common infections, SUCH AS OTITIS MEDIA AND SINUSITIS, FREQUENTLY RESOLVE SPONTANEOUSLY
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'General principles: anti-infectives' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/anti-infectives/general-principles-anti-infectives, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: BEFORE STARTING AN ANTI-INFECTIVE, TAKE A SPECIMEN FOR CULTURE AND SUSCEPTIBILITY TESTING IF APPROPRIATE
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'General principles: anti-infectives' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/anti-infectives/general-principles-anti-infectives, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: CHOOSE A DRUG WITH PROVEN EFFICACY, NARROW SPECTRUM AND FEW ADVERSE EFFECTS, THAT IS THE CHEAPEST OF THE AVAILABLE ALTERNATIVES -- NEWER, BROAD-SPECTRUM OR MORE EXPENSIVE DRUGS ARE NOT NECESSARILY BETTER
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'General principles: anti-infectives' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/anti-infectives/general-principles-anti-infectives, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: NEVER TREAT VIRAL INFECTIONS WITH ANTIBACTERIALS: THERE IS NO EVIDENCE THAT ANTIBACTERIALS PREVENT SECONDARY BACTERIAL INFECTIONS, for example in viral upper respiratory tract infection
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'General principles: anti-infectives' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/anti-infectives/general-principles-anti-infectives, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Base EMPIRICAL treatment on knowledge of LOCAL patterns of likely pathogens and LOCAL susceptibility data, and consider coverage of infrequent or resistant pathogens ONLY if clinical and other factors suggest they may be present
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'General principles: anti-infectives' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/anti-infectives/general-principles-anti-infectives, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Restrict PROPHYLAXIS to certain clinical conditions, surgical procedures with high risk of infection, or where the consequences of infection are severe such as a prosthesis
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'General principles: anti-infectives' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/anti-infectives/general-principles-anti-infectives, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH's examples of NON-SURGICAL prophylaxis: contacts of people with meningococcal or H. influenzae type b meningitis; prevention of recurrent RHEUMATIC FEVER; frequent recurrent UTIs; prevention of ENDOCARDITIS in selected instances; selected contacts of active TB; POST-SPLENECTOMY; primary and secondary prophylaxis of opportunistic infections in HIV infection; and POST-NEEDLE STICK INJURY
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'General principles: anti-infectives' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/anti-infectives/general-principles-anti-infectives, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: For SURGICAL prophylaxis, cover is NOT required for all possible pathogens; the aim is HIGH DRUG TISSUE CONCENTRATIONS AT THE TIME OF THE PROCEDURE, and SINGLE DOSES ARE USUALLY SUFFICIENT
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'General principles: anti-infectives' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/anti-infectives/general-principles-anti-infectives, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: A SECOND surgical prophylaxis dose may be required when procedures are DELAYED, when a SHORT-ACTING antibacterial such as CEFAZOLIN is used and the procedure lasts MORE THAN 3 TO 4 HOURS, or when there is EXCESSIVE BLOOD LOSS; up to 24 HOURS of prophylaxis may be required for certain indications such as some cardiac surgery
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'General principles: anti-infectives' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/anti-infectives/general-principles-anti-infectives, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Indications for COMBINATION anti-infective treatment: proven or suspected MIXED infections such as skin and soft tissue infections in diabetics where one drug cannot provide the required spectrum; where SYNERGY is required such as enterococcal endocarditis; and TO PREVENT DEVELOPMENT OF RESISTANCE, as in TB
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'General principles: anti-infectives' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/anti-infectives/general-principles-anti-infectives, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AVOID TOPICAL ANTI-INFECTIVES EXCEPT FOR EYE INFECTIONS, as sensitisation and/or selection of resistant organisms can occur, WITH THE CONSEQUENCE THAT SYSTEMIC ANTI-INFECTIVES OF THE SAME CLASS CANNOT BE USED IN SERIOUS INFECTIONS
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'General principles: anti-infectives' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/anti-infectives/general-principles-anti-infectives, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Where topical treatment is needed, PREFER agents not used systemically -- MUPIROCIN -- or ANTISEPTICS such as CHLORHEXIDINE and POVIDONE-IODINE: they have a wide spectrum, are less likely to produce sensitisation, and DO NOT PROMOTE MICROBIAL RESISTANCE
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'General principles: anti-infectives' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/anti-infectives/general-principles-anti-infectives, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMBULATORY IV treatment enables patients to complete prolonged IV treatment at home or as an outpatient, with patients usually selected and monitored by INFECTIOUS DISEASES SPECIALISTS; suitable conditions include soft tissue and bone infections, endocarditis, bacteraemia and intra-abdominal infections, and drugs requiring multiple daily doses can be given by CONTINUOUS INFUSION, for example by an elastomeric pump worn by the patient
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'General principles: anti-infectives' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/anti-infectives/general-principles-anti-infectives, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: ORAL OR RECTAL administration is adequate for most infections; exceptions are where the oral route is unavailable such as an unconscious patient, absorption is unreliable such as vomiting, or inadequate drug concentration at the site of infection would result
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'General principles: anti-infectives' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/anti-infectives/general-principles-anti-infectives, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: USUAL DOSE SCHEDULES ARE ADEQUATE FOR MOST INFECTIONS, AND IN GENERAL SICKER PEOPLE DO NOT REQUIRE HIGHER DOSES THAN PEOPLE WITH LESS SEVERE INFECTION
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'General principles: anti-infectives' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/anti-infectives/general-principles-anti-infectives, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: HIGHER doses may be necessary when the organism is proven or suspected to have REDUCED SUSCEPTIBILITY, when altered drug kinetics are likely such as crush injuries or serious burns, or when distribution to the site may be compromised -- ABSCESS (usually requires surgery or drainage), BONE, SUBARACHNOID SPACE, BRAIN, INTRACELLULAR sites such as TB, NECROTIC TISSUE, PROSTATE, SKIN, NAILS, reduced tissue perfusion such as peripheral vascular disease, CARDIAC VEGETATIONS and VITREOUS HUMOUR
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'General principles: anti-infectives' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/anti-infectives/general-principles-anti-infectives, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: THERE ARE FEW INDICATIONS FOR PROLONGED TREATMENT: generally treat until major signs and symptoms have resolved, clear clinical improvement is evident and laboratory indices trend towards normal
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'General principles: anti-infectives' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/anti-infectives/general-principles-anti-infectives, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: IF CLINICAL RESPONSE IS SLOWER THAN EXPECTED, REVIEW THE INITIAL DIAGNOSIS AND/OR TREATMENT CHOICE
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'General principles: anti-infectives' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/anti-infectives/general-principles-anti-infectives, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH's duration bands: SINGLE DOSE for candidal vulvovaginitis, intestinal worms and uncomplicated gonorrhoea; SHORT COURSE under 5 days for bacterial gastroenteritis, malaria and uncomplicated UTIs; LONGER COURSE 5 to 10 days for bacteraemia, cellulitis, chlamydial infection, intestinal amoebiasis, meningitis, peritonitis, Gram-negative, pneumococcal and Mycoplasma pneumonia, sinusitis, streptococcal pharyngitis and tonsillitis
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'General principles: anti-infectives' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/anti-infectives/general-principles-anti-infectives, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH's EXTENDED COURSE band, more than 10 days: bacterial endocarditis, deep-seated staphylococcal infection including bacteraemia, INFECTIONS IN IMMUNOCOMPROMISED PEOPLE, Legionella pneumonia, osteomyelitis, septic arthritis, pelvic inflammatory disease, prostatitis, late syphilis, TB and NEUTROPENIC FEVER
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'General principles: anti-infectives' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/anti-infectives/general-principles-anti-infectives, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: BROAD-SPECTRUM drugs affect bacterial flora MORE than narrow-spectrum drugs and are MORE LIKELY TO CAUSE GI ADVERSE EFFECTS AND SUPER-INFECTION WITH RESISTANT ORGANISMS
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'General principles: anti-infectives' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/anti-infectives/general-principles-anti-infectives, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: ANY USE OF AN ANTI-INFECTIVE ALLOWS THE DEVELOPMENT OF RESISTANCE TO IT, and depending on the mechanism resistance to other anti-infectives may also occur; MULTIDRUG RESISTANCE IN COMMON CLINICAL PATHOGENS IS A GROWING PROBLEM and WIDESPREAD AND INDISCRIMINATE USE OF BROAD-SPECTRUM ANTI-INFECTIVES IS A MAJOR CONTRIBUTOR
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'General principles: anti-infectives' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/anti-infectives/general-principles-anti-infectives, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: DRUGS THAT REMAIN THE LAST DEFENCE AGAINST MULTI-RESISTANT STRAINS SHOULD BE USED ONLY UNDER EXPERT DIRECTION: VANCOMYCIN, TEICOPLANIN, RIFAMPICIN, IMIPENEM, MEROPENEM, EXTENDED-SPECTRUM CEPHALOSPORINS AND QUINOLONES
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'General principles: anti-infectives' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/anti-infectives/general-principles-anti-infectives, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22
